The four pulls, their order, the IsWax marking and the stream they come off were already faithful. WAS: all four were force-granted and each ran its own after_obtained regardless.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): `RelicCmd.Melt` leaves the relic in `Player.Relics` as an inert entry; the port removes it from run.relics entirely
guards.issue: MECHANISM: RelicCmd.Melt (RelicCmd.cs:89-93) is `relic.Owner.MeltRelicInternal(relic); await relic.AfterRemoved();` -- the relic STAYS in the list, and the game stops it working by excluding melted relics from both hook-listener walks (RunState.cs:569 `player2.Relics.Where(r => !r.IsMelted)` for the run-level walk, CombatState.cs:428-435 for the combat walk). Its own doc comment says so: 'A melted relic remains in your inventory, but is unusable.' toy_box.py:41-42 does `run.relics.remove(wax)`, and the sim's Relic base has no is_melted member at all (EXECUTED: `hasattr(Relic, 'is_melted')` is False). EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b16.py toybox-melt`): across six combats the sim's relic count goes 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, 3 where the game's stays 5 for the whole run. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, and the reason is that every reader already filters): the hook walks exclude melted relics on both sides, so the EFFECTS agree; and every other reader of Player.Relics a ported path reaches filters on IsTradable, which itself excludes melted relics -- RanwidTheElder.cs:74/94 and RelicTrader.cs:79-124/109, mirrored at events/ranwid_the_elder.py:35/51 and events/relic_trader.py:33/38 over the sim's Relic.is_tradable (relics/base.py:189-199, whose docstring already reasons about exactly this equivalence). The only unfiltered relic-count reader in the whole game source is ILikeShiny.cs:24 (`Relics.Count >= 25`), an achievement badge and out of scope. What would make it live: porting any effect that reads the relic COUNT or the relic LIST without an IsMelted/IsTradable filter, or a conformance check that treats `len(run.relics)` as a parity signal (conformance/runner.py:1044 already samples it, to detect newly-granted relics). Filed as a gap and not a waiver because 'nothing ported observes the difference' is today's content, not the divergence's shape (binding rule 1). Rule 7: RelicCmd.cs, RunState.cs, CombatState.cs, relics/base.py, the two event files and conformance/runner.py are NOT hashed here.

guards.what: N1 (PROMPT.md bug class 13 + the sweep-A pre-diagnosis, SETTLED): `combats_seen` is never reset -- and that is CORRECT
guards.rationale: ToyBox.CombatsSeen is a [SavedProperty] (ToyBox.cs:62-79), i.e. run-scoped and persisted, and the ONLY thing AfterCombatEnd does to it is `CombatsSeen++` (ToyBox.cs:101) -- it is not a reset site. Sim relic instances live on RunState.relics and are re-attached to every CombatState, so toy_box.py's instance field is run-scoped too; a relic that melts one wax copy every third combat of the RUN would be broken by a per-combat reset. The pre-diagnosis handed to this batch describes it as 'Sweep A candidate (combats_seen; C# resets at AfterCombatEnd)', which is the PRE-REWRITE sweep-A output -- the override census that sweep-A defect 3 was about. RE-EXECUTED against the CURRENT sweep: `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-reset` now prints `toy_box ['combats_seen'] written by: combats_seen<-['__init__','after_combat_end'] C# resets: NONE (may be per-run by design)`, which agrees with the source. Also faithful: `CombatsSeen % Combats == 0` (ToyBox.cs:102) vs `self.combats_seen % self.COMBATS_PER_MELT != 0` (toy_box.py:39) -- same modulus, and the increment happens BEFORE the test on both sides, so the first melt is at combat 3 and not combat 4 (executed: combats_seen=3 is the first row where the relic count drops).

guards.what: N2 (EXECUTED): `RelicFactory.PullNextRelicFromFront(base.Owner)` x4 (ToyBox.cs:90-95) and the draws it costs
guards.rationale: The port calls run.pull_relic_from_front() four times (toy_box.py:30-31), which is the sim's transcription of the same factory method including the rarity roll off the player's Rewards stream (run.py:970-1004 and its docstring). EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b16.py toybox-melt`): the grab bag goes 96 -> 92, so all four pulls are consumed -- the failure mode audit/records/relic/calling_bell.json G2 records (three unconsumed PullNextRelicFromFront draws, `grab bag 96 -> 96`) does NOT occur here. Also faithful: `relicModel.IsWax = true` before the reward is built (ToyBox.cs:93) vs `relic.is_wax = True` before add_relic (toy_box.py:34), and the port's `if relic is None: break` handles the empty-bag case the C# `.ToMutable()` would throw on. Rule 7: run.py and audit/records/relic/calling_bell.json are not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: the wax-relic search predicate -- `r != null && r.IsWax && !r.IsMelted` (ToyBox.cs:105) vs `r.is_wax` (toy_box.py:41)
guards.rationale: Given G2's deletion, `!r.IsMelted` is automatically satisfied in the sim (a melted relic is gone), and the null check is a C# list-slot artefact. So the two searches pick the same relic in the same order -- the first wax copy in relic-list order, which is pull order -- and the four melts happen in the order the four were obtained. Recorded because the two divergences interlock: a fix for G2 that keeps melted relics in run.relics MUST add the `not r.is_melted` clause here at the same time, or the third combat would melt the same relic forever.
